newsitem.title: INDIA: India raises investment limit in small units.
newsitem.headline: India raises investment limit in small units.

text.p: The Indian cabinet decided on Friday to raise the investment ceiling in plant and machinery of small scale industrial units to 30 million rupees from the current level of six million rupees.
The cabinet also decided to reduce the export obligation of export-oriented units to 50 percent of their output from 75 percent.
India's 100 percent export oriented units are allowed to sell a part of their production in the domestic market.
Industry Minister Murasoli Maran told a news conference that the investment limit on ancillary units, currently at 7.5 million rupees, has also been raised to 30 million rupees ($838,000).

India has a list of 836 products which can be manufactured only by small-scale units, defined by the investment ceiling set by the government. Small units are also eligible for cheap credit from banks.
The government said 16 percent of cheap bank credit, mandated under central bank regulations, now goes to small industrial units.

Maran said the government increased the investment limit defining small units to offset an erosion in the value of the rupee due to inflation, a depreciation in the exchange rate of the rupee and a rise in the price of capital goods.
Tariff changes had also created conditions for a rise in the investment limit for small units, which has been revised roughly once in five years, he added.
The ceiling, which was 2.0 million rupees in 1980, was raised to 3.5 million rupees in 1985 and 6.0 million in 1991. ($1=35.8 rupees)
